title: Problem with Queries
statementMd:
You are given an array a, consisting of n integers. Your task is to process q queries of two types:

- 1 p x — set the value of the element at index p equal to x;
- 2 l r — count the number of pairs of indices (i,j) such that l≤i<j≤r and ai≠aj.

Note that the queries in this task are **encoded**; each subsequent query can only be decoded after calculating the answer to the preceding query of the second type.

## Input

The first line contains a single integer n (1≤n≤105).

The second line contains n integers a1,a2,…,an (1≤ai≤n).

The third line contains a single integer q (1≤q≤3⋅105) — the number of queries.

The next q lines describe the queries in one of the following formats:

- 1 p′ x′ (0≤p′,x′≤n−1);
- 2 l′ r′ (0≤l′,r′≤n−1).

The queries are **encoded** as follows: let last be the answer to the latest processed query of the second type (initially, last=0).

- if the type of the query is 1, then p=((p′+last)mod, x = ((x' + \mathit{last}) \bmod n) + 1.
- if the type of the query is 2, l = ((l' + \mathit{last}) \bmod n) + 1, r = ((r' + \mathit{last}) \bmod n) + 1. If l \gt r, swap their values.

**Don't forget to update the value of \mathit{last} after answering each query of the second type.**

Additional constraint on the input: there is at least one query of the second type.

## Output

For each query of the second type, print the answer — the number of pairs of indices (i, j) such that l \le i \lt j \le r and a_i \ne a_j.

## Note

In the first example, the actual queries (after decoding) are:

- `2 1 3`
- `1 1 3`
- `2 1 3`
- `1 2 3`
- `2 1 3`
